newsitem.title: INDIA: RESEARCH ALERT-India ACC net lowered-poll.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT-India ACC net lowered-poll.

text.p: Cement analysts said on Thursday they were slashing earnings forecasts for India's largest cement maker Associated Cement Companies (ACC) by an average 45 percent after its first half fell sharply below expectations.

A spot Reuter poll of six leading securities firms found they had dramatically cut ACC's 1996/97 (April-March) net profit forecast to an average 1.18 billion rupees. Their previous average forecast for the year was 2.17 billion rupees.
India's largest cement firm said late on Tuesday its net profit in the six months to September 30, 1996 fell 56 percent to 550.5 million rupees from 1.25 billion rupees a year ago.
Expectations had ranged from 800-900 million rupees.
New full year net profit estimates -- calculated after the disastrous first half results -- ranged from 800 million rupees to 1.46 billion rupees.
All analysts expected a drop in the firm's full year net from the year-ago. ACC's net profit during 1995/96 was 2.27 billion rupees.
Most analysts said they were still fine-tuning their estimates and did not want to be quoted.
They said their forecasts had not factored a hike in prices of petroleum products -- expected in the current fiscal year.
"A petrol price hike of around 10 percent would increase ACC's costs by some 100 million rupees," said an analyst at a leading Indian securities firm.

They said the price of cement in the last quarter of the fiscal would also determine full-year performance. Depressed cement prices are likely to see a slight recovery during January to March, when cement demand peaks.
Analysts said first half results had not yet been discounted in ACC's share price.

"Considering the dismal performance of the company, we believe the stock price has not yet bottomed out... we expect the stock to continue to underperform the market," said an analyst at a European brokerage.
ACC shares were trading 5.50 rupees higher at 1,023 rupees on Thursday, after crashing 12 percent on Wednesday.
ACC shares have fallen 32 percent this month in the run-up to the results.
